title.suggested: Tom Allen Goes to Law to Recover Stake Money

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that Tom Allen sued Bill Clark, final stakeholder in the Daly-McManus boxing match, for $1,000 and $750, claiming Hugh McManus won a forfeit because Dan Daly's last deposit was late.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Saturday Morning, December 8, 1888, page 6.

facts.fact: Allen backed Hugh McManus in a gloved boxing match against Dan Daly set for December 11, 1888, wagering with Daly on October 16, 1888

Allen claimed a forfeit for McManus at noon on December 5, 1888, saying Daly's final $250 deposit, due December 4 at the Globe-Democrat office, was not up; the temporary stakeholder said Daly's money was up on time
Allen sued Bill Clark, final stakeholder of the Daly-McManus match, for $1,000 he had deposited and $750 Clark received from the Globe Printing Co.; attorneys Rowe & Morris
Allen offered to let the sporting papers settle his forfeit claim
facts.quote: I am willing to leave the matter to the Clipper, the Spirit of the Times or the Police Gazette, and will abide by their decision on my claim for $750 forfeit for Hugh McManus.

notes: Suit filed 'yesterday' (December 7, 1888). Allen's card to The Republic is signed TOM ALLEN.
